newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil down on prompt surplus.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil down on prompt surplus.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps were down at midday on Wednesday on talks of surplus prompt cargoes and a weaker crude, traders said.

"The market came off this morning because of the weaker crude and an over supply for prompt cargoes," one trader said. June gas oil swaps were last quoted at $25.00/$25.10 per barrel down from Tuesday's $25.35/$25.45, brokers said.
June traded in the morning at $25.05, they said.

Traders said the market lost some ground after June Brent closed 10 cents lower to $19.62 per barrel on the International Petroleum Exchange on Monday with further loses expected after the release of bearish API data.
June WTI crude on the after hours ACCESS trading system last traded down 29 cents to $21.08 after the figures were released.
Apart from the weaker crude, the range bound physical trading also forced the swaps market to give up some of its early week gains.
Two 150,000 barrel cargoes traded on Tuesday at $25.20 per barrel and $25.40, both on free-on-board Singapore basis, both within the well defined $25.00-25.50 range.

Traders said there are about 150,000 tonnes of unsold prompt gas oil in Singapore which is keeping prices down. As a result of this, the May/June swap spread is flat while the June/July spread has narrowed to about 15 cents compared to over 60 cents on Monday.
Fuel oil was also quoted slightly weaker because of the crude with June at $100.72/$102.00, brokers said.
